subject: maths
title: Reflection and Translation on a Coordinate Grid
seo_title: Year 5 Reflection and Translation Worksheets: Mirror Lines and Moves on a Grid
standard_text: Identify, describe and represent the position of a shape following a reflection or translation, using the appropriate language, and know that the shape has not changed.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on reflection and translation: describe translations on a grid, find new coordinates, reflect points and shapes in vertical and horizontal mirror lines, and spot what stays the same. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: A translation slides a shape; a reflection flips it in a mirror line. The shape itself does not change.
key_sub: Count the squares you move, not the lines. In a reflection, each corner ends up the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side.
body_html:
Translations: slide the shape

A translation slides a shape left or right and up or down. It does not turn or flip. Every corner moves the same number of squares in the same direction.

MoveWhat changesExample from (5, 4)
right 2x gets bigger(7, 4)
left 2x gets smaller(3, 4)
up 2y gets bigger(5, 6)
down 2y gets smaller(5, 2)
Example

Describe the translation from (2, 7) to (8, 3).

Across: 2 to 8 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 squares down.

Answer: 6 squares right and 4 squares down

Reflections: flip in a mirror line

A reflection flips a shape over a mirror line. The image is a mirror image. Each corner ends up the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side.

The line x = 5 goes straight up through every point with x-coordinate 5. The line y = 4 goes straight across through every point with y-coordinate 4.

Example

Reflect (3, 4) in the mirror line x = 5.

(3, 4) is 2 squares left of the line. Go 2 squares right of the line: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4.

Answer: (7, 4)

The shape has not changed

After a translation or a reflection, the shape is in a new place, but it is the same shape and size. The side lengths, the angles, the perimeter and the area all stay the same.

TranslationReflection
What happensslidesflips in a mirror line
Which way it facesthe same waythe other way (mirror image)
Size, sides and anglesthe samethe same

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting grid lines, starting with 1 on the start lineCount the squares you jump
Reflecting by sliding: the image points the same wayFlip it: the image must face the other way
Moving the wrong way: adding for “left” or “down”Left and down make the number smaller
Stopping on the mirror line, or going past itGo the same distance on the other side
Drawing the image bigger or smallerCheck every side is the same length as before

faq.q: What do children learn about reflection and translation in Year 5?
faq.a: Year 5 pupils reflect and translate shapes on a grid in the first quadrant. They describe the new position with coordinates and the right words, and know that the shape itself has not changed.

faq.q: How do you reflect a shape in a mirror line?
faq.a: Reflect one corner at a time. Count how many squares it is from the mirror line, then count the same number on the other side. Join the new corners to draw the mirror image.

faq.q: What is the difference between a reflection and a translation?
faq.a: A translation slides a shape, so it still faces the same way. A reflection flips it in a mirror line, so the image faces the other way.

faq.q: Does a shape change size when it is translated or reflected?
faq.a: No. Only its position changes. The side lengths, angles, perimeter and area stay exactly the same.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (5, 1). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 3 to 1 is 2 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 2) and B is at (3, 6). Across: 6 to 3 is 3 squares left. Up and down: 2 to 6 is 4 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (1, 1) and B is at (7, 4). Across: 1 to 7 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 1 to 4 is 3 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (8, 7) and B is at (4, 2). Across: 8 to 4 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 7 to 2 is 5 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (3, 6) and B is at (3, 1). The x-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 6 to 1 is 5 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 5) and B is at (9, 5). Across: 2 to 9 is 7 squares right. The y-coordinate stays 5, so there is no move up or down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 5) moves to (6, 1) in B. That is 5 squares right and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 1) moves to (5, 5) in B. That is 4 squares right and 4 squares up. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (6, 5) moves to (1, 1) in B. That is 5 squares left and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 4) moves to (5, 1) in B. That is 4 squares right and 3 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (2, 6) moves to (2, 1) in B. That is 5 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (2, 7) to (8, 3). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (8, 3). Across: 2 to 8 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (9, 1) to (5, 6). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (9, 1) and the end is at (5, 6). Across: 9 to 5 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 1 to 6 is 5 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (4, 4) to (4, 9). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (4, 4) and the end is at (4, 9). The x-coordinate stays 4, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 4 to 9 is 5 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (7, 8) to (1, 8). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (7, 8) and the end is at (1, 8). Across: 7 to 1 is 6 squares left. The y-coordinate stays 8, so there is no move up or down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is at (2, 4) and point B is at (6, 4). Maya counts the grid lines from A to B, starting with 1 on A’s line. She says A moved 5 right. What is the correct translation?
items.e: Count the squares you jump, not the lines: 6 − 2 = 4. Maya counted the line A starts on, so she got 1 too many.

items.q: Kai describes the move from (1, 6) to (5, 2) as “4 right, 4 up”. What mistake did he make?
c: He should have said left, not right
He should have said down, not up
items.e: y goes from 6 to 2. It gets smaller, so the move is down: 6 − 2 = 4 down. The translation is 4 right, 4 down.

items.q: Which word means sliding a shape without turning it or flipping it?
items.e: A translation slides a shape left or right and up or down. A reflection flips it in a mirror line.

items.q: A shape is translated 3 squares left and 2 squares up. Which translation moves it back to where it started?
items.e: Undo each move: 3 left is undone by 3 right, and 2 up is undone by 2 down.

items.q: To describe the translation of a shape, which corner should you follow?
c: You must add up every corner’s move
Any corner: they all move the same way
items.e: In a translation every corner moves by the same amount in the same direction. Follow one corner and count the squares.

items.q: Point A is at (3, 4). It is translated 2 squares right and 3 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 2 squares changes x: 3 + 2 = 5. Up 3 squares changes y: 4 + 3 = 7. The new point is (5, 7).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 7). It is translated 5 squares right and 4 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. Down 4 squares changes y: 7 − 4 = 3. The new point is (7, 3).

items.q: Point A is at (8, 3). It is translated 6 squares left and 2 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 6 squares changes x: 8 − 6 = 2. Up 2 squares changes y: 3 + 2 = 5. The new point is (2, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (5, 9). It is translated 3 squares left and 6 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 3 squares changes x: 5 − 3 = 2. Down 6 squares changes y: 9 − 6 = 3. The new point is (2, 3).

items.q: Point A is at (1, 2). It is translated 6 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x stays 1. Up 6 squares changes y: 2 + 6 = 8. The new point is (1, 8).

items.q: Point A is at (9, 6). It is translated 5 squares left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 5 squares changes x: 9 − 5 = 4. y stays 6. The new point is (4, 6).

items.q: Point P is translated 4 squares right and 3 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 4 squares changes x: 2 + 4 = 6. Down 3 squares changes y: 6 − 3 = 3. The new point is (6, 3). That is point B.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 squares left and 4 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 5 squares changes x: 7 − 5 = 2. Up 4 squares changes y: 2 + 4 = 6. The new point is (2, 6). That is point D.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 squares right and 5 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 6 squares changes x: 1 + 6 = 7. Up 5 squares changes y: 1 + 5 = 6. The new point is (7, 6). That is point A.

items.q: Point P is translated 3 squares left and 5 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 3 squares changes x: 8 − 3 = 5. Down 5 squares changes y: 7 − 5 = 2. The new point is (5, 2). That is point C.

items.q: A triangle has corners at (1, 2), (4, 2) and (1, 6). It is translated 5 squares right and 1 square up. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (4, 2)?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 4 + 5 = 9. Up 1 square changes y: 2 + 1 = 3. The new point is (9, 3). Every corner moves in the same way.

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (3, 5), (8, 5), (8, 9) and (3, 9). It is translated 2 squares left and 4 squares down. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (8, 9)?
items.e: Left 2 squares changes x: 8 − 2 = 6. Down 4 squares changes y: 9 − 4 = 5. The new point is (6, 5). Every corner moves in the same way.

items.q: A square has corners at (6, 1), (9, 1), (9, 4) and (6, 4). It is translated 4 squares left and 5 squares up. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (6, 4)?
items.e: Left 4 squares changes x: 6 − 4 = 2. Up 5 squares changes y: 4 + 5 = 9. The new point is (2, 9). Every corner moves in the same way.

items.q: A triangle has corners at (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 3). It is translated 3 squares right and 4 squares up. Which list shows the new corners?
items.e: Add 3 to every x-coordinate and 4 to every y-coordinate: (2, 1) → (5, 5), (5, 1) → (8, 5), (2, 3) → (5, 7). Move every corner, not just one.

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (5, 6), (8, 6), (8, 8), (5, 8). It is translated 4 squares left and 5 squares down. Which list shows the new corners?
items.e: Take 4 from every x-coordinate and 5 from every y-coordinate. For example, (5, 6) → (1, 1) and (8, 8) → (4, 3).

items.q: Point B is translated 4 squares right and 3 squares up. It lands on (6, 8). Where did it start?
items.e: Work backwards and undo each move. 4 right is undone by 4 left: 6 − 4 = 2. 3 up is undone by 3 down: 8 − 3 = 5. B started at (2, 5).

items.q: Charlie translates (6, 4) 2 squares left and gets (8, 4). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Moving left makes the x-coordinate smaller: 6 − 2 = 4. The correct answer is (4, 4). Charlie added 2, which is a move to the right.

items.q: A point is translated left or right. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: Left and right is the x direction. The point does not move up or down, so the y-coordinate stays the same.

items.q: Point C is at (2, 6). It is translated 2 squares left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 2 changes only x: 2 − 2 = 0. y stays 6. The point lands on the y-axis at (0, 6).

items.q: Amelia translates (5, 2) 3 squares up, then 4 squares right. Where does the point end?
items.e: Do one move at a time. Up 3: (5, 5). Right 4: (9, 5). The order of the two moves does not change the end point.

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical mirror line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical mirror line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (2, 1) in the horizontal mirror line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (2, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal mirror line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 squares above the line y = 6. The image is 3 squares below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (1, 7) in the vertical mirror line x = 4. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (1, 7) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the horizontal mirror line y = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is 2 squares below the line y = 5. The image is 2 squares above it: 5 + 2 = 7. x stays 5. The image is (5, 7).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 4?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 squares above the line y = 4. The image is 2 squares below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 6?
items.e: P (8, 2) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2). That is point A. Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point C: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same row. Only C is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image is 1 square too far from the mirror line; B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it points the same way); D: the image has more squares, so its size changed.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same column. Only B is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image is 1 square too far from the mirror line; C: the shape was turned upside down, not flipped; D: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it points the same way).

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same row. Only D is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image has more squares, so its size changed; B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it points the same way); C: the shape was turned upside down, not flipped.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same column. Only A is a true mirror image. Others: B: the image has more squares, so its size changed; C: the shape was turned upside down, not flipped; D: the image is 1 square too far from the mirror line.

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the vertical mirror line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is on the mirror line x = 5, so it does not move: (5, 3). A point on the mirror line is its own reflection.

items.q: A point is reflected in a horizontal mirror line. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: A horizontal mirror line goes across. The point flips up or down over it, so only y changes. x stays the same.

items.q: Point P is 3 squares to the left of a vertical mirror line. Where is its image?
c: 3 squares to the left of the line
3 squares to the right of the line
6 squares to the right of the line
4 squares to the right of the line
items.e: In a reflection the image is the same distance from the mirror line as the point, on the other side.

items.q: Poppy reflects a right-angled triangle in a vertical mirror line. Her image points the same way as the triangle. What mistake did she make?
c: She slid it instead of flipping it
items.e: A reflection is a mirror image, so it faces the other way. If the image points the same way, the shape was slid (translated).

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 5), (1, 5). It is reflected in the vertical mirror line x = 4. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (1, 5)?
items.e: The corner (1, 5) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 5. The image is (7, 5).

sets.title: Translation or reflection? The shape has not changed

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B points the same way as A. Every corner moved 5 squares right and 3 squares up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4). That is a translation.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A: the foot of the L points the other way. It is a reflection in the line x = 5. The size has not changed.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every corner moved 5 squares left and 2 squares up. That is a translation.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is A flipped upside down over the line y = 4: the right angle is now at the top. That is a reflection.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: The sides of A are 2 squares long. The sides of B are 4 squares long. A translation or a reflection never changes the size.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: A is 4 squares by 2 squares. B is only 2 squares by 1 square, so B is smaller. It is not a translation or a reflection.

items.q: Ava wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it is too far from the line
No: it was slid, not flipped
items.e: Each corner of B is the same distance from the line x = 5 as its partner in A: (1, 2) is 4 squares left of the line and (9, 2) is 4 squares right. B is correct.

items.q: Freya wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it is too far from the line
No: it was slid, not flipped
items.e: (1, 1) is 3 squares below the line y = 4, so its image should be 3 squares above, at (1, 7). B is at (1, 8): 1 square too far.

items.q: Evie wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it is too far from the line
No: it was slid, not flipped
items.e: In A the sloping side is on the right. In B it is also on the right, so B points the same way: it was slid. A mirror image would have the sloping side on the left.

items.q: Grace wants to reflect shape A in the dashed mirror line. Is shape B correct?
c: No: it is too far from the line
No: it was slid, not flipped
items.e: The sides of A are 2 squares long, but the sides of B are 3 squares long. A reflection never changes the size.

items.q: A triangle with corners at (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4) moves to (5, 1), (7, 1), (5, 4). What happened?
items.e: Every corner moved 4 squares right and the y-coordinates stayed the same. The triangle faces the same way: a translation.

items.q: A triangle with corners at (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4) moves to (7, 1), (5, 1), (7, 4). What happened?
items.e: (1, 1) moved 6 squares but (3, 1) moved only 2, so it is not a slide. Each corner is the same distance from x = 4 on the other side: a reflection in the line x = 4.

items.q: A rectangle is 4 squares long and 2 squares wide. It is translated 3 squares right. How long is the image?
items.e: A translation only moves the shape. It does not stretch it, so the image is still 4 squares long and 2 squares wide.

items.q: A triangle has an angle of 35°. The triangle is reflected in a mirror line. What is that angle in the image?
items.e: A reflection flips the shape but does not change it. Every angle stays the same, so the angle is still 35°.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 14 cm. It is translated 5 cm to the right. What is the perimeter of the image?
items.e: The sides do not change length when a shape slides, so the perimeter stays 14 cm. The 5 cm is how far it moved, not a side.

items.q: Which of these changes when a shape is translated?
items.e: A translation moves the shape to a new place. The size, side lengths and angles stay the same.

items.q: Which sentence is true after a reflection?
c: The image faces the same way
The image is bigger than the shape
The image is the same size, but flipped
items.e: A reflection makes a mirror image. It faces the other way, but its size, sides and angles have not changed.

items.q: Harry reflects a shape. He says the image is smaller because it is further from (0, 0). Is he right?
c: Only if the mirror line is far away
No: a reflection never changes the size
items.e: Moving a shape to a new place does not change its size. Count the squares along each side: they are the same.

items.q: A right-angled triangle is reflected in a mirror line. Does the image have a right angle?
c: Only if the shape is translated
No: the right angle is lost
Only if the mirror line is vertical
Yes: the angles stay the same
items.e: Reflecting flips the triangle, but every angle stays the same size. The right angle is still a right angle, it just faces the other way.

items.q: How can you tell a reflection from a translation?
c: A translation is always further away
A translation is always upside down
A reflection is flipped; a translation faces the same way
items.e: Both keep the size and the angles. In a translation the shape slides and still points the same way. In a reflection it is a mirror image.

items.q: The plan shows Amelia’s bedroom: a bed, a desk and a wardrobe (W). The bed is translated 4 squares right. What are the new coordinates of its bottom-left corner?
items.e: The bottom-left corner of the bed is at (1, 4). Right 4 changes only x: 1 + 4 = 5. The corner moves to (5, 4).

items.q: The plan shows Amelia’s bedroom: a bed, a desk and a wardrobe (W). The desk is translated so that its bottom-left corner is at (2, 1). Describe the translation.
items.e: The corner is at (6, 1) and the new corner is at (2, 1). Across: 6 to 2 is 4 squares left. The y-coordinate stays 1, so there is no move up or down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: The plan shows Amelia’s bedroom: a bed, a desk and a wardrobe (W). The wardrobe is translated 3 squares left and 1 square down. What are the new coordinates of its top-left corner?
items.e: The top-left corner of the wardrobe is at (7, 8). Left 3: 7 − 3 = 4. Down 1: 8 − 1 = 7. It moves to (4, 7).

items.q: The plan shows Amelia’s bedroom: a bed, a desk and a wardrobe (W). Amelia moves the bed. Its corners are now at (4, 3), (6, 3), (6, 7), (4, 7). Describe the translation.
items.e: The bottom-left corner of the bed is at (1, 4) and the new corner is at (4, 3). Across: 1 to 4 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 4 to 3 is 1 square down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: In a board game, Arjun’s counter is at (2, 3). He moves it 5 squares right and 4 squares up. Where does it land?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. Up 4 squares changes y: 3 + 4 = 7. The new point is (7, 7).

items.q: In a board game, Mohammed’s counter moves from (6, 6) to (1, 2). Describe the move.
items.e: The start is at (6, 6) and the end is at (1, 2). Across: 6 to 1 is 5 squares left. Up and down: 6 to 2 is 4 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: In a game, each turn moves a counter 3 squares right or 3 squares up. Aisha’s counter starts at (1, 1). She has 2 turns right and 1 turn up. Where is the counter now?
items.e: 2 turns right is 2 × 3 = 6 squares right: 1 + 6 = 7. 1 turn up is 3 squares up: 1 + 3 = 4. The counter is at (7, 4).

items.q: In a computing lesson, Alfie’s robot starts at (2, 5). It moves 4 squares right, then 3 squares down, then 1 square left. Where does it stop?
items.e: Follow one move at a time. Right 4: (6, 5). Down 3: (6, 2). Left 1: (5, 2).

items.q: On a game board, a counter at (1, 6) is reflected in the vertical mirror line x = 4. Where does it land?
items.e: The counter at (1, 6) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 6. The image is (7, 6).

items.q: Half of a logo is drawn. The whole logo is symmetrical in the mirror line x = 5. Which corner on the right matches the corner at (1, 4)?
items.e: The corner (1, 4) is 4 squares to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 4 squares to the right of it: 5 + 4 = 9. y stays 4. The image is (9, 4). (5, 4) is what you get by sliding the half across instead of flipping it.

items.q: Half of a logo is drawn. The whole logo is symmetrical in the mirror line x = 5. Which corner on the right matches the corner at (3, 7)?
items.e: The corner (3, 7) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Half of a logo is drawn. The whole logo is symmetrical in the mirror line x = 5. How many squares wide is the whole logo?
items.e: The half goes from x = 1 to the mirror line at x = 5: 4 squares. The other half is the same, so 4 + 4 = 8 squares. Count squares, not lines (that gives 9).

items.q: A school logo is reflected in the horizontal mirror line y = 5 to make a pattern. Where does the corner at (3, 2) go?
items.e: The corner (3, 2) is 3 squares below the line y = 5. The image is 3 squares above it: 5 + 3 = 8. x stays 3. The image is (3, 8).

items.q: Ruby draws a house shape with its roof point at (2, 7). She reflects the house in the mirror line x = 6. Where is the roof point of the image?
items.e: The roof point (2, 7) is 4 squares to the left of the line x = 6. The image is 4 squares to the right of it: 6 + 4 = 10. y stays 7. The image is (10, 7).

items.q: A shop sign is reflected in the mirror line x = 3. Where does the corner at (5, 6) go?
items.e: The corner (5, 6) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 3. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 3 − 2 = 1. y stays 6. The image is (1, 6).

items.q: A row of tiles is made by translating a tile 3 squares right each time. The first tile has a corner at (1, 2). Where is that corner on the 3rd tile?
items.e: Tile 1: (1, 2). Tile 2 is one move: (4, 2). Tile 3 is two moves: 1 + 3 + 3 = 7, so (7, 2). There are only 2 moves to get to the 3rd tile.

items.q: On a map, a lorry drives from (1, 5) to (8, 5), then 3 squares down. Where is it now?
items.e: From (1, 5) to (8, 5) only x changes. Then down 3: 5 − 3 = 2. The lorry is at (8, 2).

items.q: A garden has a path along the line x = 5. A pond with corners at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 4), (1, 4) is reflected in the path to make a matching pond. Which list shows the corners of the new pond?
items.e: Each corner goes the same distance on the other side of x = 5: (1, 2) is 4 squares left, so its image is 4 squares right at (9, 2). (3, 2) is 2 squares left, so its image is (7, 2).

items.q: In a game, a counter at (7, 3) is reflected in the horizontal line y = 4, then translated 2 squares left. Where does it end?
items.e: Reflect first: (7, 3) is 1 square below y = 4, so the image is 1 square above, at (7, 5). Then left 2: 7 − 2 = 5. It ends at (5, 5).

items.q: A rug is 3 squares long and 2 squares wide. It is translated 4 squares across the floor plan. How many squares does it cover now?
items.e: The rug covers 3 × 2 = 6 squares. A translation does not change the size, so it still covers 6 squares.
